extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs and treaty text
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article reporting the signing and full text excerpts of the Statute of the Netherlands–Indonesian Union, plus related news items on military, diplomatic and economic arrangements. It combines reportage of events with publication of treaty articles and explanatory commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification requirement for transfer of sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereignty resolution must be ratified by the Dutch and Indonesian Parliaments and by the representative bodies of the other fifteen constituent states of the republic of the U.S.I.; if one should refuse, these decisions would be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Dutch agreed 'unconditionally and irrevocably' to transfer complete sovereignty to the young republic not later than Dec. 30, provided the Dutch and Indonesian parliaments approve. They must vote on the decisions within six weeks. Dr. Drees expressed confidence of parliamentary ratification by the necessary two-thirds vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military withdrawal and naval-base arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for withdrawal of all Dutch troops from Indonesia within the first six months of 1950 if shipping space permits; a one-year limit was set for withdrawal of the Dutch navy; the great naval base at Sceraja (Java) will remain provisionally under the Dutch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Indonesia finally emerges as completely independent the base will have a Dutch commander responsible to the Indonesian government under the Indonesian flag. The United Nations Conciliation Commission will co-operate in the withdrawal of Dutch forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of the Union — voluntariness, equality, independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kingdom of the Netherlands and the Republic of the United States of Indonesia, having decided on a basis of voluntariness, equality and complete independence to call into being a friendly cooperation with each other ... to create the Netherlands Indonesian Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 1 establishes that the partners have equal status and that nothing in the statute shall be interpreted as excluding cooperation in fields not mentioned, without prejudice to each partner's status as an independent and sovereign state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Union — fields of cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union aims at cooperation of the partners for the promotion of their common interests. This cooperation shall take place with respect to matters lying primarily in the field of foreign relations and defense and as far as necessary finance and also economic and cultural nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 2: cooperation primarily concerns foreign relations and defense, and may extend into finance, economic and cultural areas as necessary. Specific provisions for these fields are set forth in agreements attached to the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of the Union — person and succession/temporary incapacity provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: At the head of the Union shall be Her Majesty Queen Juliana, Princess of Orange Nassau, and in case of succession her lawful successors to the crown of the Netherlands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5 includes provisions for minority, inability or temporary cessation of the head's duties: both partners shall make necessary provisions by common agreement. Article 6 states the head embodies the concept of voluntary and lasting cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking: common consent and ratification of joint regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions in the Union shall be taken in agreement between the two partners. Decisions taken by the conference of ministers for the enactment of joint regulations require ratification by the respective Parliaments of the partners; after ratification the head of the Union shall state that agreement exists and the joint regulation shall be promulgated in the official statute books of each partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint regulations thereby gain force of law in each partner. For other decisions the head of the Union, upon request of the conference, may state that agreement exists; procedural routes for dealing with decisions are outlined in Article 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functioning of the Union — conferences and ministerial participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conferences shall be held twice each year and further as often as the partners shall deem necessary, between the ministers thereto assigned by the partners or between persons vested with equal or similar responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise agreed, three ministers of each partner will participate. Ministers remain responsible to their respective organs on the basis of their constitutions. The conference may institute committees with parity of appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary contacts and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The two partners shall establish a good contact and a regular cooperation between the respective Parliaments of the partners. The first discussion between the representatives of the Parliaments shall take place within eight months after the coming into being of the Provisional Parliament of the Republic of the United States of Indonesia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10 prescribes timelines for initial parliamentary engagement to foster legislative cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent secretariat and rotation of secretaries-general
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union is served by a permanent secretariat. Each of the partners appoints a secretary-general, each of whom takes charge of the secretariat by yearly rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other personnel is appointed in agreement between the two secretaries-general in accordance with an instruction drawn up jointly by the partners (Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Union Court of Arbitration — jurisdiction and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a Union Court of Arbitration for the settlement of matters of law and justice in the name of the head of the Union. The Court shall take cognizance of legal disputes arising out of the Union Statute, out of any agreement between the partners or out of joint regulations, and brought before the Court by one of the partners against the other — or jointly by both partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 13 defines the Court's remit to decide disputes related to the statute, agreements and joint regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union Court of Arbitration — composition, terms and oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union Court of Arbitration consists of three members appointed by the Kingdom of the Netherlands and three members appointed by the Republic of the United States of Indonesia. The members of the Court are appointed for a period of ten years. They shall resign once they reach the age of sixty-five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to taking up office members shall take the oath or make the promise in accordance with their religious faith before the head of the Union to fulfill their office honestly, scrupulously and impartially (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Union Court — decision rules and tie procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union Court of Arbitration decides by a majority of votes. In case votes are equally divided the Court shall, unless the two partners otherwise request, call upon the president of the International Court of Justice or another international authority to appoint a person of another nationality as an extraordinary member of the Union Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an extraordinary member is appointed, that member shall take part in a renewed consideration of the dispute and in the decision thereon. Further procedural rules shall be established by joint regulation or, until then, by the Court itself (Articles 15–16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with Court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The two partners undertake to comply with the decisions of the Union Court of Arbitration and to implement decisions under their own authority and responsibility each within his own territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 17 places implementation responsibility on each partner within its own jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supremacy of Union Statute and joint regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of conflict between provisions of the law of the partners ... on the one side and the Union Statute or any agreement between the partners or a joint regulation on the other, the latter category of provisions shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 18 establishes the primacy of the Statute, agreements and joint regulations over conflicting internal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to seek international adjudication outside the Union Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The two partners reserve all their rights under international law or otherwise to solicit the decision of an international judge or arbitrator in cases where both partners consider that the Union Court of Arbitration lacks competence or in cases where the Court declares itself incompetent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 preserves recourse to other international fora where the Union Court is found to lack competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields with separate attached agreements (foreign, defense, financial, cultural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions concerning the cooperation between the partners in the field of foreign relations, defense, financial and economic relations, and cultural relations are set forth in the agreements attached to the present Statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 20–23 indicate that detailed arrangements for these functional areas are provided in attached agreements rather than in the core Statute text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and treatment of nationals within partner territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Without prejudice to arrangements regarding political and other rights, the nationality of citizens of one partner shall not constitute an objection with regard to holding offices within the jurisdiction of the other partner, except for (1) offices responsible to a representative assembly and (2) political, authoritative, judicial and leading offices specified by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners must appreciate the special interests of the citizens and corporate bodies of the other partner and avoid appreciable discrimination; treatment shall not be less favorable than that accorded to citizens and corporate bodies of a third state, subject to regulations for protection of national interests or economically weak groups (Article 24 and Citizenship section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions — high commissioners as diplomatic representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: To further the interests of the partners within each other's territory, the governments of the partners shall appoint high commissioners. These shall have the status of diplomatic representatives with the rank of ambassador.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 25 creates a diplomatic mechanism to represent partner interests in each other's territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union financing — expense sharing and interim arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed each partner shall bear one half of the expenses of the Union. Further provisions in respect of the expenses of the Union shall be established in common agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until establishment of such common agreement the conference of ministers shall make the necessary provisions (Article 26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official texts, languages and UN registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All official documents issued by the conference of ministers or by other Union organs shall be in the Netherlands and Indonesian languages. The Union Statute and agreements may be presented to the Secretariat of the United Nations for registration in accordance with Article 102 of the Charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 27–28 address bilingual authenticity and provide for UN registration of the Statute and agreements.
